title: Online, two moves: the networked round trip that reaches its peer over a network
why: Online is the second networked mode, and the store owes it everything it owes the first: one commit per accepted move, a local side that survives the close although no byte of the archive carries it, and an Undo refused because a retraction between two players is their agreement rather than one device's decision. A mode that reached the store as Free Play would keep no local side and would offer the undo. It names no golden: its document differs from the nearby one in the mode string alone, and the archive corpus states each rule once rather than twice.
